bullets.title: WeCroak
bullets.note: (**[**iOS**](https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/wecroak/id1248149943?mt=8)**,** [**Android**](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.kkitcreations.wecroak)**).** Description: “The WeCroak app is inspired by a Bhutanese folk saying: to be a happy person, one must contemplate death five times daily.” This app sends you five prompts per day to stop and think about death, each complete with a related quote. I love how social sharing is disabled. Thank you to Josh T. and Matt M. for the recommendation.

bullets.title: Kokoyakyu: High School Baseball
bullets.note: This documentary really brings back the memories. It tracks high school competitors and coaches in one of Japan’s deepest passions: baseball. The school uniforms, practices, buildings, customs, etc. are all nearly exactly what I experienced as a 15-year-old exchange student in Tokyo. [_Natsukashii naaaa_](https://www.bbc.com/travel/article/20200119-a-uniquely-japanese-take-on-nostalgia#:~:text=Natsukashii%20is%20a%20Japanese%20word,fond%20memory%20from%20your%20past.&text=But%20natsukashii%20%E2%80%93%20which%20derives%20from,desire%20to%20return%20to%20it.)! Deep bow to reader Ethan Jacobs ([@ethanajacobs](https://twitter.com/ethanajacobs/status/1415729968793927683)) for the suggestion.

bullets.title: Terence McKenna’s Memes
bullets.note: (_VICE_). I first read Terence McKenna when I was 15 and 16 years old, reading [_The Archaic Revival_](https://www.amazon.com/Archaic-Revival-Speculations-Psychedelic-Mushrooms/dp/0062506137/ref=sr_1_1?dchild=1&keywords=the+archaic+revival&qid=1626384158&sr=8-1) and [_Food of the Gods_](https://www.amazon.com/Food-Gods-Original-Knowledge-Evolution/dp/0553371304/ref=pd_vtp_1/147-3319022-5415553?pd_rd_w=XSpGa&pf_rd_p=016e3697-91be-4dc2-9533-ef9350e7e73d&pf_rd_r=JR7WJ73AZ606GHC4RQG8&pd_rd_r=9bc56b9a-19e5-4c3c-be89-9032bc01c940&pd_rd_wg=G2y9x&pd_rd_i=0553371304&psc=1), respectively. Both had an impact on my trajectory. The Irish bard of psychedelics loved wordsmithing and enjoyed controversy. Two of my favorite memes from the above linked article are _Worry is preposterous; we don’t know enough to worry_ and _Nature is not mute; it is man who is deaf_.
